response.query: What sensitivity-analysis grid (ranges for false-match/missed-match) and bounding approaches should be pre-registered to assess linkage-driven bias?
response.answer: Sensitivity-analysis grids should cover false-match and missed-match ranges from 0% to 100%, with bounding approaches using extreme values to assess linkage-driven bias.

results.title: Predicting effective microRNA target sites in mammalian ...
results.content: We compared the predictive performance of our context++ model to that of the most recent versions of 17 in silico tools for predicting miRNA targets, including AnTar (Wen et al., 2011), DIANA-microT-CDS (Reczko et al., 2012), ElMMo (Gaidatzis et al., 2007), MBSTAR (Bandyopadhyay et al., 2015), miRanda-MicroCosm (Griffiths-Jones et al., 2008), miRmap (Vejnar and Zdobnov, 2012), mirSVR (Betel et al., 2010), miRTarget2 (Wang and El Naqa, 2008), MIRZA-G (Gumienny and Zavolan, 2015), PACCMIT-CDS (Marin et al., 2013), PicTar2 implemented for predictions conserved through mammals, chicken, or fish (PicTarM, PicTarC, and PicTarF, respectively) (Anders et al., 2012), PITA (Kertesz et al., 2007), RNA22 (Miranda et al., 2006), SVMicrO (Liu et al., 2010), TargetRank (Nielsen et al., 2007), and TargetSpy (Sturm et al., 2010); as well as successive versions of TargetScan, which offer context scores (Grimson et al., 2007), *P*CT scores (Friedman et al., 2009), or context+ scores (Garcia et al., 2011) as options for ranking predictions (TargetScan5, TargetScan.PCT, or TargetScan6, respectively) for either all mRNAs with a canonical 7–8 nt 3′-UTR site (TargetScan.All) or those with only broadly conserved sites (TargetScan.Cons).
